sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Wholesale Physical Arbitrage of Grade A Refined Copper Cathodes

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Panama – Republic of Panama (single unitary national jurisdiction, no sub-state fiscal differentiation)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romano-Germanic) with strong Anglo-American influence in trust, banking, and maritime commercial law
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Panama–United States Trade Promotion Agreement (Investment Chapter; in force since 31 October 2012)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 23 of 27 April 2015 (AML/CFT framework), as reformed by Law 70 of 2019 and Law 254 of 2021; Executive Decree 406 of 2 November 2019 (consolidated AML/CFT regulations); Law 52 of 2016 (Beneficial Ownership Registry); Law 129 of 2020 (beneficial ownership and tax information reforms); Law 25 of 12 June 1995 (Private Interest Foundations), as amended by Law 158 of 2016; SBP Rule 004-2017 (banking KYC/CDD standards); UAF regulations (suspicious transaction reporting).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Foundation Charter (Acta de Fundación) and Extract (Certificado de Fundación) – notarized originals for registration and third-party exhibits
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public of the Panamanian Civil Circuit; thereafter certified by the Registro Público de Panamá
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Panama is a Contracting State to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention; Apostilles issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs – Oficina de Legalizaciones y Apostillas)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the registered Foundation Charter (Copia Certificada de la Inscripción) evidencing public-registry inscription
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for Apostille member states; consular legalization via Panamanian consulate for non-member states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing and no-encumbrance certificate (Paz y Salvo de la fundación)
Registered Agent Acceptance and Incumbency Certificate (constituting the resident agent, council members, and secretary)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed Panamanian attorney / regulated corporate services provider
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille (or consular legalization when the counterparty registry is a non-Apostille state)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial Owner (UBO) Declaration and Foundation AML/KYC file (source of funds and source of wealth proofs for the statutory US$10,000 endowment)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registered Agent and compliance officer of the Private Interest Foundation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Internal compliance certification; notarization and apostille required only when the file is submitted to foreign banks or LME ring-dealing counterparties

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Founder identity and due-diligence bundle (certified passport copies, corporate charters of upstream entities, powers of attorney)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public and/or competent authority in the founder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the origin state is an Apostille member; otherwise full consular legalization chain (Ministry of Foreign Affairs of origin + Panamanian Consulate)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all foundation founders, council members, protectors, and UBOs against OFAC SDN and sectoral sanctions lists, UN Security Council consolidated list, EU and UK consolidated sanctions lists, and Panamanian national restrictive lists, plus PEP databases (domestic, foreign, and international-organization PEPs) with enhanced monitoring for at least five (5) years after office exit. Enhanced due diligence applies per SBP Rule 004-2017 and Executive Decree 406/2019, including source-of-funds and source-of-wealth evidence for the statutory US$10,000 minimum endowment, adverse-media screening, and LME/LC payment-rail concentration-risk review. Red flags specific to ISIC 4662 (copper cathodes) include metal origin from OFAC-sanctioned or high-risk jurisdictions (e.g., Iran, Syria, Russia, and occupied territories), structured documentary LC drawings, and third-party LME warrant transfers unsupported by independent shipping and warehousing documentation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá – Trámites en Línea (online name reservation module for legal persons), administered by the Dirección General de Registro of the Registro Público (https://www.registropublico.gob.pa); name availability may also be verified through the Panamá Emprende single-window portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The Foundation Charter must be executed and registered in Spanish (a bilingual Spanish-English version is permissible with the Spanish text controlling for registry interpretation). The foundation's name must be renderable in Latin script; foreign-script names must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet for inscription. Per Law 25 of 1995, the registered name must contain the denomination 'Fundación de Interés Privado' or the abbreviation 'PIF' to evidence the entity type, and must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered Panamanian legal entity.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Words suggesting state, sovereign, or institutional character: 'Nacional', 'Gobierno', 'Estado', 'Ministerio', 'Gobernación', 'Municipal', 'República' (require express government authorization or are absolutely prohibited)

Financial-sector terms implying regulated activity without prior SBP licensing: 'Banco', 'Seguro', 'Reaseguro', 'Financiera', 'Casa de Valores', 'Fondo de Inversión', 'Sociedad de Ahorro', 'Cooperativa', 'Trust', 'Fideicomiso'
Terms reserved for regulated insurance, gaming, mining, and hydrocarbons activities outside the ISIC 4662 wholesale-trading scope
Identical or deceptively similar names to any existing corporation, foundation, or limited liability company inscribed in the Registro Público de Panamá
Suffixes evoking other entity types such as 'S.A.', 'Sociedad Anónima', 'Corp.', or 'Limited'; the required suffix is 'Fundación de Interés Privado' or 'PIF'
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registro Público rejects the proposed name (for identity, similarity, or prohibited-token grounds), the applicant may file a 'Recurso de Reconsideración' with the Dirección General del Registro Público within five (5) business days of the rejection notice, attaching a legal opinion on non-confusing distinctiveness and up to three alternative names; a denied reconsideration may be appealed via 'Recurso de Apelación' to the administrative jurisdiction and ultimately the Contentious-Administrative Chamber of the Supreme Court of Justice. An approved but unused reservation may be extended for one additional 30-day period upon payment of the renewal tariff before the initial 30-day window lapses.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is statutorily permissible for a PIF because the registered office coincides with the licensed resident agent's Panamanian address and the foundation is not required to lease physical premises. However, for wholesale copper cathode trading with documentary LC and LME warrant payment rails, banks and commodity counterparties applying SBP Rule 004-2017 substance expectations will require either (i) a real operational footprint through an affiliated trading company, or (ii) a documented commercial-substance narrative (warehouse receipts, trade finance lines, personnel, and physical flow contracts) before opening accounts, confirming LCs, or accepting warrant transfers.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (~10–15% annual probability). Unannounced on-site inspections by the UAF, SBP, or the Registro Público would target the resident agent's office and its UBO/AML files rather than the foundation's premises, because the PIF itself maintains no physical trading office; the risk increases if the foundation is named in a suspicious transaction report or if OFAC/UAF sanctions red flags attach to copper cathode counterparties.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name reservation and clearance fee (online search and reservation of 'Fundación de Interés Privado' name)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff of the Registro Público fee schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of Foundation Charter (Acta de Fundación) and notarial certifications
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary Public of the Civil Circuit, Panama City
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial statutory tariff and prevailing market notarial fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Public Registry inscription fee for the Private Interest Foundation (capital band up to US$10,000)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registration tariff based on foundation capital band

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille authentication of certified charter and registered-agent documents (two document sets)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Panama – Oficina de Legalizaciones y Apostillas
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-document apostille tariff, prevailing market rate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered agent and registered office services (first full year)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Panamanian law firm / regulated corporate services provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market annual retainer for PIF resident-agent service

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal drafting of Foundation Charter, internal Regulations (Reglamento), and council/director appointments
Beneficial Ownership (UBO) registry filing and initial AML/KYC/PEP file setup
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registered Agent / Compliance Officer of the foundation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Compliance package market rate (UBO declaration, sanctions screening, file custody)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certificate of Good Standing and no-encumbrance certificate (two certified public-registry certificates)
Certified Spanish translation of founder identity documents and corporate charters of upstream entities
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark per-page translation and certification fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Initial statutory foundation endowment (minimum capital) – contributed to the foundation treasury
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Foundation treasury (founder contribution; registered agent custody)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory minimum under Law 25 of 1995 (Article 8) – US$10,000 or equivalent assets

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley No. 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 on Private Interest Foundations, as amended by Ley No. 13 de 2002 and Executive Decree No. 3 de 2002; Articles 1, 2, 4, 6, 7, 13, 15, 18, 19, 21 and 40 govern formation, endowment, the Foundation Council, the Protector and supplementary corporate rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Departamento de Fundaciones de Interés Privado (Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acta de Constitución (Foundation Charter) – executed as a public deed (escritura pública) or protocolized private instrument before a Panamanian Notary Public and inscribed in the Public Registry of Panama.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The Foundation Charter must state an initial endowment of at least USD 10,000 or its equivalent in another currency, contributed in cash or in kind and fully assigned to the foundation's purposes. No blocked escrow account is required under Panamanian law, but the endowment must be identifiable in the foundation's records and the performance or contribution must be evidenced at inscription.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF THE PRIVATE INTEREST FOUNDATION. The Foundation Council, validly convened and constituting a quorum, unanimously resolves: (1) Ratification: the Foundation Charter inscribed before the Public Registry of Panama is ratified in full, and the initial endowment is accepted as contributed by the Founder. (2) Registered Office: the registered office is fixed at Avenida Samuel Lewis, Obarrio, Panama City, Republic of Panama. (3) Officers: [Name] is appointed President, [Name] Secretary and [Name] Treasurer of the Foundation Council, each to serve until removal or successor appointment. (4) Administration: the Secretary shall file the notarized excerpts with the Public Registry and pay all registration charges. There being no further business, the meeting is declared adjourned.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting of Foundation Charter and Name Availability Search
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Departamento de Fundaciones de Interés Privado (preliminary name search service)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a licensed Panamanian attorney to draft the Acta de Constitución containing all mandatory clauses of Law 25 de 1995: foundation name with 'Fundación' or 'Fundation' suffix, foundation purpose (wholesale trading of non-ferrous metals and copper cathodes), registered office in Panama, initial endowment of at least USD 10,000, Foundation Council members, Protector (optional), beneficiaries and duration. Submit a name availability request to the Registry and obtain the Certificado de Búsqueda de Nombre.
required_dossiers: Proposed foundation name and three alternatives
Draft Foundation Charter prepared by counsel
Passport copies and domicile evidence of the Founder
Statement of initial endowment and asset contribution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered entity, file a new name search request with an alternative name; no substantive fee is lost beyond the search tariff.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarial Execution and Legalization of the Foundation Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública de la República de Panamá (Notary Public of Panama)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Founder(s) appear before a Panamanian Notary Public and execute the Acta de Constitución. The notary verifies identity and capacity, witnesses the signature, and issues the first testimoniam (Testimonio de la Escritura Pública) together with the protocolized copy required for registry filing. If any founder executes outside Panama, the signature must be authenticated by apostille or consular legalization.
required_dossiers: Approved Foundation Charter
Original name availability certificate
Valid passport of each founder and council member
Power of attorney if the Founder is represented
Apostilled or consular-legalized signatures (for foreign execution)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary rejects a clause for inconsistency with law, amend the draft and re-execute a corrective instrument (rectificación notarial) prior to registry filing; the resignation or replacement of a founder is recorded by marginal note.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of Official Fees, Stamp Taxes and Registry Tariffs
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Banco Nacional de Panamá and Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) collection windows
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Compute the applicable Impuesto de Timbre and the Public Registry inscription right based on the declared endowment and the official tariff table. Deliver the stamped declaration forms and make payment into the Tesoro Nacional through the authorized bank. Attach the official receipts and stamped forms to the inscription dossier submitted to the Registry.
required_dossiers: Stamp tax declaration (Formulario de Impuesto de Timbre)
Registry inscription fee receipt
Notarized copy of the Foundation Charter
Power of attorney for the applicant attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: In case of underpayment, settle the differential amount plus the statutory surcharge within the term indicated by DGI; in case of overpayment, request a credit note or refund through the DGI refund procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscription in the Registry of Private Interest Foundations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Departamento de Fundaciones de Interés Privado
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Testimonio de la Escritura Pública together with the fee receipts and the stamped documents. The Registry examines formal compliance with Law 25 de 1995, assigns the foundation inscription number, and issues the certificate of inscription. Legal personality of the foundation commences on the date of inscription, and the foundation may then open bank accounts and execute contracts.
required_dossiers: First testimonial of the public deed of foundation
Payment receipts for registry fees and stamp taxes
Notarized acceptance of office by the Foundation Council members
Registered office declaration with exact address in Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues reparos (observations), correct the deficiency through a notarial clarification deed or marginal note within the statutory term; if registration is refused, file a reconsideration appeal before the Directorate General of the Public Registry or a judicial action before the Third Chamber of the Supreme Court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Taxpayer Registration (RUC), Municipal Aviso de Operación and Bank Account Opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) and Municipio de Panamá – Dirección de Gestión de Ingresos
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After inscription, obtain the Registro Único de Contribuyente (RUC/NIT) for the foundation, then apply to the Municipality of Panama for the Aviso de Operación covering the commercial activity ISIC 4662 (wholesale of non-ferrous metals). Present the certificate of inscription, lease agreement of the office, and the RUC registration receipt. Open a corporate bank account with the certified copy of the foundation deed and the RUC certificate.
required_dossiers: Certificate of inscription from the Public Registry
RUC application form signed by the legal representative
Lease agreement or proof of premises
Aviso de Operación application and municipal fee receipt
Bank account opening questionnaire and beneficial ownership declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Municipality rejects the Aviso for incorrect activity classification, resubmit with corrected ISIC 4662 wording; if DGI delays RUC issuance, escalate via written request to the Head of the Registro de Contribuyentes; bank refusal may be overcome by presenting the notarized foundation deed and a UAF-compliant ownership chart.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Governance Activation, AML Compliance and Foundation Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) and the foundation's Registered Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Activate the Foundation Council's statutory book, maintain minutes of council resolutions, and instruct the registered agent to retain the beneficial ownership register and up-to-date records of the foundation's copper cathode trading operations, including LME warrant transfers and documentary LC settlements. If the foundation becomes subject to UAF obligations as a legal vehicle, file the annual economic information return and any suspicious transaction reports.
required_dossiers: Foundation Council minutes and appointment records
Beneficial ownership register
AML policy and risk assessment manual
Statement of traded commodities and payment rails (LME warrants, LCs)
Registered agent acceptance and annual fees receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If UAF requests further information, submit the supplementary declarations within the granted extension; failure to maintain the statutory register is cured by filing late entries with a sworn explanation and paying the late-filing tariff before the Public Registry.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) – mandatory industrial operating license is not required for wholesale trading of non-ferrous metals (ISIC 4662); the only operative local authorization is the Aviso de Operación issued by the Municipio de Panamá.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación / Licencia Comercial Municipal (non-industrial commercial license for wholesale metal trading)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) – Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Registration not required – activity is wholesale distribution of refined copper cathodes with no physical processing plant, effluent discharge or land disturbance in Panama
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to pure merchant trading; general obligations under Ley No. 41 de 1998 (Ley General del Ambiente) and Ley No. 55 de 2003 for solid waste segregation and disposal; no wastewater, VOC or particulate thresholds triggered in the absence of industrial operations; minimal compliance only for office and warehousing waste manifests.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá fire safety certificate for the registered office and any bonded warehouse; municipal structural occupancy clearance (permiso de uso de suelo y ocupación) from the Municipio de Panamá; compliance with MITRADEL occupational health and safety standards (Resolución No. 347 de 2009) including fire extinguishers, emergency signage, first-aid kit and non-hazardous material handling protocol for copper cathode storage.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF), Panama; electronic portal: Sede Electrónica de la DGI (www.dgi.gob.pa)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity must appoint a resident legal representative and obtain a Panama Tax Identification Number (RUC – Registro Único de Contribuyente) through the DGI's Sede Electrónica or at the DGI taxpayer service window, presenting the foundation charter, identity documents of the founder and officers, and proof of a local registered agent or domicile; the RUC is issued after validation of the application and, where applicable, confirmation of the economic activity code (ISIC 4662) and registration in the Comisión Nacional de Valores or other ancillary registers if required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama generally applies territorial taxation; a PIF may elect to be treated as a separate taxable person for tax purposes, but the standard default is pass-through or transparent treatment under Special Law 25 of 1995; no formal check-the-box election exists; taxpayers may file an annual sworn statement (Declaración Jurada) electing to report only Panamanian-source income and may opt into the Multinational Headquarters (SEM) regime or special regimes where available; hybrid mismatch elections are limited and subject to General Directorate of Revenues criteria.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Impuesto a la Transferencia de Bienes Corporales Muebles y Servicios – ITBMS)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Annual taxable gross turnover exceeding USD 300,000 (or as established by DGI regulations; registration is required for persons engaging in taxable activities, with a simplified registration for occasional imports or services).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama mandates electronic invoicing and fiscal clearance through the DGI's 'Facturación Electrónica' system; authorized e-invoice issuers must use DGI-certified software, transmit invoices in the specified XML/JSON format through the Sede Electrónica API, and incorporate the digital stamp (código de seguridad) and validation QR element before issuance to buyers; real-time validation applies for large taxpayers, with deferred validation for smaller or newly registered taxpayers.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods and certain offshore services are zero-rated for ITBMS purposes; eligibility requires proving that the goods physically leave Panama or that the service is provided wholly for use outside Panama; the seller must issue an export invoice indicating zero-rate, maintain transport evidence, and obtain the DGI export certificate; copper cathodes exported via port or bonded warehouse may qualify if shipped under customs export procedures.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación Electrónica, comprising forma DUA / manifiesto)
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical departure from Panama
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank/LC transfer records proving payment received from abroad
Purchase invoice or LME warrant documentation supporting acquisition of the copper cathodes
DGI export certification and, if applicable, Free Trade Zone or warehouse movement documents
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGI may audit export documentation including customs records, shipping manifests, and FX reconciliation; false zero-rating declarations or failure to prove physical export can result in retroactive assessment of ITBMS at 7%, late interest, fines up to 100% of the omitted tax, administrative penalties under the Tax Code and Código Fiscal, and criminal prosecution for tax fraud; transfer-pricing and economic-substance documentation may also be required for SEM or free zone entities.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Panama has no autonomous central bank. Monetary authority is the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) for banking supervision; the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF) and the Superintendencia del Mercado de Valores (SMV) oversee financial policy and securities matters. The U.S. dollar is sole legal tender; the balboa (PAB) is a nominal monetary unit circulating only as divisional coins pegged 1:1 to USD.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility for both current and capital account transactions, as Panama operates a dollarized monetary system without exchange control legislation. Profit remittances and capital repatriation are unrestricted; however, all transfers are subject to Panama’s anti-money laundering (AML), counter-financing of terrorism (CFT) and know-your-client (KYC) rules, including mandatory reporting of suspicious transactions to the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF). No prior central bank approval is required for trade-related cross-border payments or dividend distributions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export proceeds surrender or mandatory conversion ratios exist under Panamanian law. Exporters of physical commodities such as copper cathodes may freely hold, disburse, or reinvest USD proceeds. Compliance obligations are limited to accounting transparency, tax reporting under the territorial tax system, and AML/CFT record-keeping for international transfers exceeding USD 10,000 or structuring thresholds.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (USD current account) and segregated Escrow Account for contract settlements

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banco Nacional de Panamá (National Bank of Panama)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (USD) for state-related contracts; Capital Escrow Account subject to public bank compliance review
Operational Account and dedicated Trade Finance Account with electronic banking and LC facilities
Operational Account; Escrow Account for advance payment guarantees
Operational Account and FX/trade clearing sub-account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility for offshore digital EMIs as primary banking solution. Panama does not issue electronic money institution (EMI) licenses under a standalone framework; firms offering e-money or mass payment services must be licensed by the SBP under the Panamanian Banking Law (Legislative Decree 2 of 2008) or operate under the Fintech Innovation Hub regime. A PIF held by a non-resident would face heightened due diligence when attempting to transact through an unlicensed foreign fintech, and the SBP will treat unregistered EMIs as shadow financial service providers. Use of such a fintech is viable only as a secondary payment corridor with strict AML-name screening and after due diligence on the EMI’s underlying banking partnerships.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of the foundation’s council members and beneficial owners is generally required for first-time account opening at tier-1 Panamanian banks. Certain international private banks permit remote opening via notarized apostilled powers of attorney and enhanced video-KYC, but the final signatory and the compliance officer still require at least one physical interview (in person at the bank’s Panama City headquarters or at a designated regional office). For a PIF trading in non-ferrous copper, banks apply a de facto mandate for two directors or the appointed beneficiary to appear in person and produce original foundation charter, certificate of incumbency, and valid passports.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PIF beneficiary is undisclosed or benefits from bearer share instruments
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the Foundation Charter and Foundation Council resolution identifying all beneficiaries; notarized declaration of beneficial ownership; registry certificate from the Public Registry of Panama showing the PIF’s registered agent and council members; latest financial statements; CVs and business references of the council members.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk geography: copper cathode trading with customers in sanctioned or high-risk jurisdictions, or involving transshipment via third countries
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full know-your-supplier and know-your-customer (KYS/KYC) file: passport copies, corporate registry extracts (e.g., Chile, Peru, Brazil, US, EU), business licenses, warehouse receipts and LME warrants, bill-of-lading drafts, and an Esquematic Chart of the physical flow including vessel names and port of discharge. Provide a sanctions screening report from an independent provider (e.g., Dow Jones, Refinitiv, World-Check) with false-positive explanations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transactions showing rapid inbound/outbound movements (pass-through funds) without underlying trade evidence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete trade documentation package: purchase contract, sales contract, invoice, packing list, certificate of analysis (CoA), insurance policy, and LME settlement statement. For hedging transactions, include master agreement, forward contract confirmation, and margin call schedule. Provide an explanation memorandum connecting each movement to a specific commercial lot.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual use of third-party payment intermediaries or NRA/PIF-to-PIF transfers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written authorization by the PIF council naming the intermediary; due diligence on the intermediary (license, owner, FATCA/GIIN); chain-of-title documents for the copper (original impositor/concentrator sales contract, refinery certificate, and warehouse transfer deed); evidence that the intermediary’s fee is commercially reasonable and tied to a genuine trade facilitation service.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Usable rails are USD-denominated wire transfers through the Clearing House Interbank Payments System (CHIPS) or Fedwire for US-based correspondent banks, and SWIFT MT103/202 for Europe and Asia. Recommended routing: parent/shareholder bank → correspondent in Panama or the PIF’s bank in Panama with purpose code TRADE/FINANCING (e.g., 'Grants or capital contribution to a foundation', 'Trade receivable', or 'Payment for goods and services' under the IMF/OECD BPM6 classification). The remitter must include the PIF’s full legal name, account number, and a reference to the original copper purchase contract. For capital injections, a board resolution of the PIF must be provided to the bank, together with the notarized source-of-funds statement, to avoid AML flagging. All inbound capital should be booked as 'capital contribution' or 'trust beneficiary advancement' in local accounting ledgers.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails will be (a) SWIFT MT103 for payment of copper suppliers and logistics providers using standard purpose codes (e.g., '1101 - Trade in goods', '1111 - Trade in services'), (b) Commercial Documentary Letters of Credit (LC) issued via MT700, MT707 amendments, and advised through the exporter’s bank for purchases of copper cathodes from producers or large traders, and (c) LME Warrant transfer through registered warehouse receipts, with settlement via online payment at the LME clearing house (LMEclear) for brokers. Domestic Panamanian disbursements are processed through Central de Riesgo (SCR) for luca pepper? Actually through local ACH (ACH Panama – Sistema de Pagos de Alto Valor, SPAV) for USD transfers or direct SWIFT for amounts over USD 10,000, but the preferred commercial rail remains the USD wire/Fedwire/CHIPS rail through correspondent banks. Disbursement instructions must always identify the shipment files and require dual signatures; the bank will request evidence of the physical delivery and customs clearance to prevent trade-based laundering.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Since the PIF’s commercial invoices are in USD and Panama uses USD, no USD/PAB forward is necessary; although a nominal balboa currency exists, it is pegged at exactly 1:1 and offers no hedging value.

Forward contracts and NDFs in USD/EUR or USD/JPY may be used to hedge treasury cash flows when the PIF holds receivables or payables in non-USD currencies; these are permitted via Banco General, Multibank, or global investment banks after ISDA/SBP-compliant documentation.

Cross-currency swaps (USD against another commodity settlement currency) are permissible under SBP regulations for non-financial customers, requiring the PIF to sign a master agreement and post adequate margin.

Commodity swap agreements and copper price forward/option contracts (cleared through LMEclear or OTC with qualified counterparties) are permitted as true commercial hedging instruments tied to physical copper cathode positions; they are not considered speculative trading by the Panamanian banking supervisor providing the volume corresponds to the PIF’s trade turnover.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Flat Tax for Private Interest Foundations (Tasa Anual de las Fundaciones de Interés Privado / Annual Franchise Tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance, Republic of Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 30 April; no filing extension is available in the DGI registered-agent portal.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late penalty of USD 50 per month or fraction of a month overdue plus statutory interest; persistent non-payment for two consecutive years results in loss of good standing, suspension of rights before the Public Registry, and administrative strike-off after the required notice period.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Final Beneficial Owner Confirmation (Declaración Jurada / Informe Anual de Beneficiario Final)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) — Final Beneficial Owner Registry, Republic of Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within the first quarter, generally by 31 March, based on the position as of 31 December of the preceding year; material changes in founder, Foundation Council, protectors, or final beneficiaries must be reported within 30 days of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unfiled or inaccurate UBO information exposes the PIF and the registered agent to administrative fines, suspension of good-standing certificates, and enhanced AML scrutiny by the Financial Intelligence Unit; continued default may lead to mandatory deregistration from the Public Registry.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No independent statutory audit is automatically required for a Panama Private Interest Foundation under Law 25 of 1995. A certified audit becomes mandatory if (i) the Foundation Charter or Reglamento expressly requires an annual audit; (ii) the DGI classifies the PIF as a large taxpayer and imposes audited financial statements for Panama-source income tax purposes; or (iii) the PIF is consolidated into an IFRS reporting group.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as issued by the IASB; IFRS for SMEs may be used where the PIF is not publicly accountable. Panamanian generally accepted accounting principles are aligned with IFRS for regulated reporting purposes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: A Panama Private Interest Foundation has no shareholders; therefore there is no share-transfer register filing. The resident agent must annually verify the current roster of final beneficial owners and file the required confirmation with the DGI by 31 March. Any transfer of foundation beneficial interests or beneficiary certificates is recorded in the private Register of Beneficial Interests; if the transfer changes the Foundation Charter, a notarized amendment must be presented to the Public Registry of Panama.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Foundation Council Members (Roster and Appointments)
Minute Book of Foundation Council Resolutions
Register of Beneficial Interests / Beneficiary Certificates (if issued)
Final Beneficial Owner Register maintained by the resident agent under AML Law 23 of 2015

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 950 – USD 2,200 per annum (registered agent, government fee handling, statutory register custody, and annual UBO compliance)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,200 – USD 3,500 per engagement if an elective or tax-driven IFRS / IFRS-for-SMEs audit is required; nil if no audit mandate arises

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% on net Panama-source income; territorial scope excludes foreign-source income unless remitted to a Panama permanent establishment.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holiday. A Private Interest Foundation operating solely as an asset-holding vehicle without Panama-source commercial income can achieve effective zero tax through the territorial exclusion. Preferential deductions exist for reinvested profits in approved tourism, reforestation, and Colon Free Zone exporter regimes, but not for wholesale copper cathode arbitrage.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 1221 Declaración de Renta de Personas Jurídicas (Corporate Income Tax Return) filed through the DGI Sede Electrónica portal (T@-Pago).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year entity, on or before 31 March of the following year. Taxpayers eligible for digital payment extension may obtain an additional two months by request.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registro Único de Contribuyente (RUC) tax identification number and entity legal name.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign-foundation owner without Panama tax nexus must not be listed as the taxpayer; the Panamanian legal entity (PIF) itself files under its own RUC, and the beneficiary appears only in the beneficial ownership annex.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross receipts from Panama-source sale of goods, including commissions earned by an agent or trading intermediary located in Panama.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only revenues attributable to a Panama establishment or to activities performed in Panama. If the copper cathode sale is negotiated, documented, and closed entirely abroad with no Panama permanent establishment, enter zero here and provide a geographic-source memorandum.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign-source income claimed as excluded under territorial taxation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PIFs must be prepared to substantiate that title transfers, LME warrant delivery, and buyer/seller risk passed outside Panama. Bare invoicing from Panama is insufficient and will be reclassified as Panama-source.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible costs and expenses directly and necessarily incurred in generating Panama-source revenue, including ocean freight and LME warehouse charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only costs contractually borne by the Panamanian entity and backed by invoices from the counterparty are deductible; intra-group service charges without economic substance are disallowed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Arm's-length adjustments for controlled related-party transactions; declaration of transfer pricing appendices.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose all related-party sales to non-resident affiliates in full, even if the income is claimed as foreign-source. A non-resident beneficial owner acting as principal must not be conflated with the PIF reporting entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses carried forward from prior years, subject to the 5-year limitation and annual registered tax basis value.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses arising from foreign-source activities may not be offset against Panama-source profits; loss schedules must identify the geographic source with supporting customs and banking records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable Panama-source income after deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident PIF with only unmanaged passive shareholding, net taxable income is nil. If a Panama trading office is used, the full margin on the commodity arbitrage is attributed to that office.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax at 25% on net taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Computed only on Panama-source income; no tax is due on dividends or distributions of foreign-source profits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Alternative Minimum Tax (IMT) where applicable at the higher of the regular computation and 0.75% of gross assets or 4% of gross taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PIFs with no Panama gross assets and no Panama-source income must file the IMT schedule with zero values; failure to file still triggers the late-return penalty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Signature of resident director or licensed CPA representing the foundation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign owner cannot sign; the notification must include a representante legal domiciled in Panama. Electronic signature via the DGI portal is accepted after RUC activation by a local attorney-in-fact.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a fine of USD 50 to USD 2,500 depending on net equities, plus monthly surcharge of 0.5% on the tax due. Failure to file after formal notice gives rise to an automatic assessment and a criminal fine equivalent to 3 times the omitted tax where the amount exceeds USD 5,000.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 5% withholding on dividends or foundation distributions paid from profits that have borne the 25% corporate tax; 10% on distributions from profits exempted or benefited at the corporate level; 0% on distributions of profits derived from foreign-source income under Panama's territorial model where no Panama-source earnings are distributed.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced withholding under an applicable Double Tax Agreement, the beneficial owner must (i) obtain a Tax Residence Certificate from the counterparty jurisdiction, (ii) submit the completed DGI Form 1225-S to the withholding agent or paying fund, and (iii) retain a declaration of beneficial ownership and no-conduit status. Treaty reductions require advance submission before issuance of distribution; retroactive refund claims use Form 1221-R and are statute-limited to three years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on royalties for trademarks, patents, and technical assistance rendered abroad is 12.5%; non-banking loan interest paid to non-residents is 12.5%, and bank interest payable to foreign financial institutions is 5%. Under Panama's network of DTAs, royalty and interest WHT may be reduced to 5–10% for residents of treaty partners, subject to TRC and beneficial-ownership filing.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File and Master File are required where annual related-party transactions exceed USD 2 million, or where consolidated group revenues of the ultimate parent exceed USD 100 million and Panama operations conduct cross-border controlled transactions. Overview/two-line TP disclosure is required for all controlled transactions above USD 250,000.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama Law 254 of 2020 applies Economic Substance Regulations to entities carrying on 'relevant activities' from within Panama. Wholesale commodity trading is a relevant activity when the PIF is managed, directed, or staffed in Panama. Such an entity must evidence a local office, local board meetings, qualified employees, and strategic risk management in Panama. A PIF relying solely on offshore status while exercising management from Panama is exposed to full re-characterization and the associated tax.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Deliberate Territorial Source Misdeclaration
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Recording a copper cathode LME arbitrage profit as foreign-source despite contract negotiation, risk-taking, and delivery instructions being managed by a Panama-registered PIF office. Fabricating a foreign intermediary to strip Panama-source margin or submitting false invoices to reduce taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalty of 40% of the omitted tax plus 1% monthly interest; administrative fine up to USD 200,000; criminal tax fraud constitutes imprisonment from one to five years under the Criminal Tax Procedure Code.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed false returns or directed the misdeclaration are jointly and severally liable for the corporation's unreported tax. Courts may issue a travel ban preventing exit from Panama pending restitution, order civil attachment of personal assets, and impose disqualification from serving on any Panamanian company for up to five years; imprisonment applies to the criminal conviction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Violation of Economic Substance Requirements (Shell Company Masking)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The PIF is presented as a tax-neutral foundation for copper trading, with registered agent in Panama, but all directors are non-resident, no Panamanian bank account exists, and risk management is performed remotely. Tax authorities reclassify the entity as managed-in-Panama.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fine from USD 2,500 to USD 75,000 per annum; immediate re-assessment at the 25% statutory rate on previously excluded foreign-source revenue; 50% surcharge for false declaration and possible dissolution of the foundation by the Registro Público.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Foundation council members are civilly liable for the amount of tax found deficient to the extent they approved unlawful distributions. Directors may be subject to asset freezing orders, 90-day temporary travel suspension, and criminal indictment for criminal conspiracy where the foundation was deliberately designed to obstruct tax collection.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Misstatement and Base Erosion Through Related-Party Sourcing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling refined copper cathodes to a related non-resident trading firm at a discount below the LME cash-settlement price without performing a comparable analysis, or paying excessive management fees to a foreign affiliated entity for non-existent advisory services.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Portfolio transfer pricing adjustment to the arm's-length price, collection of the underpaid tax plus interest at 4.5% semi-annual accumulative, and a misstatement penalty of 30% of the corrected deficiency for a 'serious' infraction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed the transfer pricing declaration without verifying economic substance hold personal civil liability for 50% of the assessed deficiency. The Panama Tax Court may order a director's professional license suspension for two years, and a criminal penalty applies if false documentation is supplied to the DGI.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML-Compliance Failure in Commodity Arbitrage Payment Rails
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Executing LME warrant transfers and documentary letter-of-credit payments through the PIF's bank account without verifying beneficial ownership of the counterparty, or accepting third-party remittances that are used to settle copper cathode transactions outside the formal banking system. The AML risk tier for base metal trading is Medium-Risk Enhanced.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Panama's AML Law 23 of 2015 authorizes fines of up to USD 1 million or 10% of the gross value of the suspicious transactions, whichever is greater; a licensed PIF agent may have that authorization revoked with immediate asset freezes in connection with the transaction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers who knowingly process fraudulent commodity trades are personally indictable for money laundering predicated on tax evasion; penalty in Panama is five to ten years of imprisonment and permanent removal from the natural person registry of regulated commercial agents.
